messages:
sophie_support: Heads-up — customer-facing p99 spike on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 starting ~2024-11-05T10:15Z. Several tenants seeing timeouts and 503s. p95 jumped from ~350ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~12s. Request IDs: r-9a1c, r-9a2f, r-9a44. Can someone triage? :eyes:

anil_sre: On it. Any recent deploys to runtime or autoscaler events?

sophie_support: No customer deploys. We did push a runtime rollout last night to eu-west but rollout shows as successful. Console shows admitted queue depth climbing and a lot of 'admit_time' > 2000ms logs.

maria_runtime: Looking at traces — long wait in admission/queue before worker dispatch. KV cache hit rates normal. Seems worker pools saturated. Which model and batch config?

sophie_support: Model: redwood-xl-1, seq len 1024 typical. Batch target 32, concurrency per-worker 2. Route: default-prod-eu.

anil_sre: Can you paste the admission logs around a failing request? grep for "admit" and "queued". Also check worker pod restart count.

sophie_support: Paste of a sample from logs:
```
2024-11-05T10:17:10Z admit: request_id=r-9a1c queued_ms=734 queue_pos=36
2024-11-05T10:17:11Z dispatch: worker=ri-worker-7 delay_ms=732 exec_ms=12000
2024-11-05T10:17:23Z error: request_id=r-9a1c status=504 timeout
```

oliver_oncall: worker exec_ms=12000 — that matches the p99. Are we seeing single large batches causing long tail? Check batch sizes in traces.

maria_runtime: Batch sizes spiking to 96 because of over-batching on long-seq jobs. The runtime tried to fill batches and didn't honor per-request latency SLO. Admission allowed big batches. That's triggering head-of-line blocking for short jobs.

anil_sre: Root cause hypothesis: admission policy is prioritizing throughput; when traffic surged, long seq requests get packed and slow down everyone. Also maybe a worker oom/restart reduced effective parallelism. Any pod restarts?

sophie_support: One worker pod evicted in eu-west-1b at 10:12 — kube events show transient OOM. Replica count is 8 but desired is 10 (autoscaler didn't scale up).

oliver_oncall: Possible mitigations (short-term): 1) Lower max_batch_size for redwood-xl-1 route to 48; 2) Enforce per-request max_batch_wait_ms=20ms; 3) Temporarily route latency-sensitive tenants to redwood-xl-1-quant (faster small-batch variant) or redwood-medium-1 fallback; 4) Increase worker replicas to 12 manually; 5) Enable admit-tiered-priority to favor short requests. Which do we want to try first?

anil_sre: I'll manually scale workers to 12 in eu-west and disable the old autoscaler cooldown to allow immediate scale. Also will cordon/evict the evicted node to avoid repeat OOMs.

maria_runtime: I'll hotpatch route config to set max_batch_size=48 and max_batch_wait_ms=25 for default-prod-eu. Patch will be rolled to 10% canary then 100% within 2m.

sophie_support: Deploy-bot: any auto-scaling events or anomalies?

deploy-bot: AUTO-SCALE: scaling redwood-runtime-eu-west from 8 -> 12 replicas triggered by manual action by anil_sre at 2024-11-05T10:28:33Z.

oliver_oncall: After scale and patch, watch p95/p99 for next 15 minutes. Also add a rule to admission controller: "prefer small batches when queue depth > 50". We should rollback throughput-optimized policy that was enabled last night.

maria_runtime: Added route patch and admission rule change. Canary metrics look promising: at canary p99 dropped to 2.1s, p95 to 420ms. Rolling to 100% now.

anil_sre: Node eviction root cause looked like a memory leak in an older worker binary; I'll trigger rolling restart of remaining workers after scale completes to pick up patched binary.

sophie_support: Noted. Customers reporting fewer errors now (acme-prod confirms). Keeping this thread open for post-mortem.

oliver_oncall: Next steps: 1) postmortem draft (assignment: anil_sre + maria_runtime), 2) revert throughput flag in runtime-config, 3) add regression alert on p99 > 5s with sustained queue depth > 30, 4) run a small canary load test simulating long-seq jobs.

sophie_support: Thanks all. I'll update customer tickets and patch notes. :white_check_mark:

maria_runtime: Quick repro steps for PM: run workload generator with 10% long-seq (1024) and 90% short (128), 1000 qps for 10m, observe tails; repro script: 
```bash
./loadgen --qps 1000 --mix "short:0.9:128,long:0.1:1024" --route default-prod-eu --duration 600s
```

anil_sre: Adding postmortem items: fix memory leak, tweak autoscaler thresholds, add admission policy unit tests.

sophie_support: Closing thread when postmortem posted. Great triage, team.
